content.text: bisphosphonates may be considered for pain in early CRPS, esp w abnormal bone scans; small RCTs: alendronate, neridronate and clodronate can ↓pain, w generally mild SE; consider serious risks: ONJ, esophageal ulceration.

CI: abnormalities of the esophagus which delay esophageal emptying such as stricture or achalasia. CI: inability to stand or sit upright for at least 30 min. CI: hypocalcemia. Esophageal reactions (esophagitis, ulcers, erosions) reported; be alert for signs and instruct pts to discontinue and seek medical attention for dysphagia, odynophagia, retrosternal pain, or new/worsening heartburn. Hypocalcemia must be corrected b4 initiating therapy. Severe bone, joint, muscle pain may occur; discontinue use if severe symptoms develop. ONJ reported (can occur spontaneously; generally associated w/ tooth extraction and/or local infection w/ delayed healing). Atypical fractures incl femoral fractures reported; pts w/ new thigh or groin pain should be evaluated to rule out a femoral fracture; re-evaluate risk/benefit and consider interrupting bisphosphonate therapy. Not recommended if CrCl less than 35 mL/min. Calcium, antacids, or oral medications containing multivalent cations interfere w/ absorption; instruct pts to wait at least one-half hour after FOSAMAX b4 any other oral medication. OD: hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and upper GI adverse events may result; give milk or antacids to bind alendronate; ⍉ induce vomiting (risk of esophageal irritation); keep the pt fully upright.
